preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 10
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 10) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(N == int(line.split()[0]) and N >= 1 and N <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after T is an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5) representing the length of array A.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == N and all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains N space-separated integers A_i (1 ≤ A_i ≤ 10^5) representing the elements of array A.
In each array A, no element appears more than twice (frequency of each element is at most 2).

postconditions.description: The output consists of T test cases, each producing two lines: the first line is the maximum Hamming distance, and the second line is the array B.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == N for line in stdout.splitlines()[2::2])
postconditions.description: For each test case, the second line of output contains exactly N space-separated integers representing array B.

postconditions.expression: all(all(x in A for x in B) for A, B in zip([list(map(int, stdin.splitlines()[2*i+1].split())) for i in range(T)], [list(map(int, stdout.splitlines()[2*i+2].split())) for i in range(T)]))
postconditions.description: Array B is a permutation (shuffling) of array A for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(sum(1 for i in range(N) if A[i] != B[i]) == int(stdout.splitlines()[2*i+1]) for i, (A, B) in enumerate(zip([list(map(int, stdin.splitlines()[2*i+1].split())) for i in range(T)], [list(map(int, stdout.splitlines()[2*i+2].split())) for i in range(T)])))
postconditions.description: The Hamming distance between A and B is maximized for each test case.
